newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana invites bids for state sugar firm.
newsitem.headline: Ghana invites bids for state sugar firm.

text.p: Ghana has put its state-owned sugar plantations and refineries up for sale and set a deadline of June 12 for submission of bids by international investors, a privatisation document said.

Ghana Sugar Estates Ltd (GHASEL) runs two sugar cane estates near Accra with a total of 9,970 hectares but refineries, one at each site, were closed in 1983 and are now largely obsolete, a privatisation memorandum from the government, obtained by Reuters, said.
At peak production, Ghasel produced an average of 11,800 tonnes of refined sugar, 13,000 tonnes of molasses and 12,000 tonnes of alcohol, said the memorandum.
Both plantations had reverted to natural vegetation or were being used for subsistence farming and cattle raising.
The 7,580 hectare freehold Asutsuare Estate, 100 km east of Accra, has irrigation links to the River Volta, a Czech-built refinery and a functioning distillery.
The 2,390 hectare leasehold Komenda estate, 150 km east of Accra, includes a Polish-built refinery.
Sugar cane farming at Komenda had been unsuccessful for climatological and other reasons but both plantations up for sale were suitable for other high-value cash crops, the memorandum said.
Investors should submit letters of interest by May 15 but would be given until June 12 for submission of bids.
